newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says will appeal if it loses US computer case.
newsitem.headline: NEC says will appeal if it loses US computer case.

text.p: NEC Corp said on Wednesday that it plans to appeal if a U.S. federal court turns down its request to suspend a Commerce Department anti-dumping investigation involving NEC supercomputers.
"We would appeal to an upper court," NEC executive vice president Masao Toka told a news conference.
The investigation began after Cray Computer Corp accused NEC of dumping - or selling at deep discounts to achieve market share - supercomputing equipment in the United States.
Toka said he did not know if there was a possibility that NEC would be able to reach a compromise with Cray.

NEC said on Tuesday that it and its U.S. subsidiary, HNSX Supercomputers Inc, filed a suit in the Court of International Trade in New York seeking a suspension of a Commerce Department anti-dumping investigation.
NEC said it wants the investigation suspended and is asking for an impartial third party to handle the case.
